reason: The text explicitly demonstrates Yahweh's intention to help the Hebrew people through multiple elements: (1) God commands Moses and Aaron to tell Pharaoh 'Let my people go' (שַׁלַּח אֶת־עַמִּי); (2) God repeatedly promises to liberate them and drive them out of Egypt בְיָד חֲזָקָה (with a strong hand); (3) During the plagues, God protects the Hebrews—their land (Goshen) is spared from hail, frogs, and locusts; (4) God explicitly shields their livestock while Egypt's livestock dies (וְהִפְלָה יְהוָה בֵּין מִקְנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל); (5) The entire narrative arc shows God actively working to free them from slavery. While the text also reveals God's intention to demonstrate His power and spread His name, helping the Hebrew people is unambiguously presented as one of Yahweh's central goals in this passage.
